newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stock market continues to break records. [CORRECTED 16:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stock market continues to break records. [CORRECTED 16:50 GMT]

text.p: Bulls continued their rampage on Zimbabwe's stock market on Monday with the main industrial index rising 1.8 percent to push through the key 10,000 barrier for the first time in the market's 51-year history.
But dealers warned that the market was beginning to look toppish and that share purchases would slow.

On Monday the 57-counter index shot up 174.67 points to end the day at 10,006.20 as local investors continued to buy aggressively amid softening money market rates and predictions of higher growth this year for Zimbabwe's agro-based economy.
"We knew the market would shoot up to 10,000 but we don't see it going any further now. It should be correcting," one broker said.
"It is already showing signs of reduced momentum with softness creeping into some second-tier stocks," another one said.

Leading Monday's winners, blue-chip beverages and supermarkets conglomerate Delta leapt 200 cents to 4,700 as did cigarette manufacturer Rothmans to 6,000 (corrects from 4,700), clothing retailer Edgars surged 150 cents to 4,500 and bankers Barclays jumped 100 cents to 3,200.

Winery Cairns rose 40 cents to 1,400, finance house UDC gained 30 cents to 330, transport group Clan climbed 25 cents to 550, steel window manufacturer Radar added 20 cents to 430 and hotel chain Zimsum put on 10 cents to 440.

Against the trend, furniture and clothing retailer Tedco dropped 80 cents to 1,200, horticulture company Ariston shed 40 cents to 2,360, clothing retailer Truworths lost 30 cents to 1,250 in reasonable turnover while rubber products-maker Acacia, pharmaceutical group Caps and construction firm Marshall shed 10 cents to 350, 370 and 280 respectively.

Minings were also active with gold producer Ashanti shooting up 1,000 cents to 9,000 while Rio Tinto, another gold counter, and Wankie Colliery lost 10 cents each to 2,800 and 610. Gold investor Falcon fel 175 cents to 1,025 dragging the seven-share mining index 7.41 points lower to end at 1,147.16.
